newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - FRANCE - LE MONDE JULY 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FRANCE - LE MONDE JULY 2.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.

-- President Jacques Chirac holds a series of meetings with former conservative ministers and ousted parliamentarians to reimpose his authority on the defeated centre-right parties after last month's election, won by the left.

Certain conservative leaders, which the paper does not name, are studying April 1998 as the earliest legally possible date for a new parliamentary election, or else are looking at the "hypothetical" possibility of an early presidential election.

-- The Socialist party's annual congress in November will be more difficult than anticipated for Prime Minister Lionel Jospin amid outcry from sections of the party over Renault's decision to go ahead with its plan to close a Belgian car plant.
-- European political and central bank leaders nervously await the results of France's public audit, due this month -- seen as one of the last major hurdles to monetary union.
-- Soaring stock exchange shows faith in European recovery.

-- French car manufacturers, facing a slump in sales, turn their backs on past incentives to stimulate demand, such as the new-cars-for-old rebates offered by the previous conservative govvernment -- the schemes merely brought forward purchases leading to painful after-effects.
-- Bouygues and Veba in telecommunications deal.
-- France and Britain agree on Eurotunnel licence extension on conditions but indicate for the first time that could not prevent any future takeover by creditor banks.
